verses.57:2: {vere} falais justiça: * julgai {recta}, filhos dos homens.
verses.57:3: Pois no coração praticais iniquidades: * na terra as vossas mãos tramam injustiças.
verses.57:5: {furor} da serpente: * {aspidis} da áspide surda, e que tapa os seus ouvidos,
verses.57:6: Que não escutará a voz dos {incantantium}: * {venefici} que {incantantis} sabiamente.
verses.57:7: Deus quebrará os dentes deles {inore}: * o Senhor {confringet} {molas} dos leões.
verses.57:8: {devenient} como a água {decurrens}: * {intendit} o seu arco até que enfraqueçam.
verses.57:9: Como a cera que {fluit}, {auferentur}: * caiu fogo {supercecidit}, e não viram o sol.
verses.57:10: Antes que os vossos espinhos {intellegerent} {rhamnum}: * {viventes}, assim na ira os {absorbet}.
verses.57:11: O justo se alegrará {viderit} a vingança: * lavará as suas mãos no sangue do pecador.
verses.57:12: E o homem dirá: Se {utique1} há fruto para o justo: * {utique2} há {deus12} que os julga na terra.

decisions.why: Two adverbs in a row, *vere útique* (ἀληθῶς ἄρα): 'truly' and the particle 'indeed / then'. *útique* comes back twice in 57:12, where it frames the psalm's last line, so it wants one Portuguese word in all three places: *de fato*. *vere* is kept as its own word by turning it into the clause *é … verdade que* (grammar, D2). Dropping *útique* here (MS1932 *Se verdadeiramente falais*, DRB 'If in very deed') would lose the echo that closes the psalm.

options.label: Se é de fato verdade que

forms.vere: Se é de fato verdade que

options.label: Se de fato verdadeiramente
options.note: both adverbs as adverbs; heavy, eight syllables of adverb.

options.label: Se verdadeiramente
options.note: MS1932; *útique* not rendered, the echo with 57:12 lost.

decisions.why: *recta* is a neuter plural object (DRB 'judge right things'); the Greek εὐθεῖα κρίνετε reads as well as an adverbial neuter plural, 'judge uprightly'. The first colon has a content object (*justítiam loquímini* → *falais justiça*, as the *loqui mendácium* row keeps its content), so the object could be kept for the parallel; but *julgai o que é reto* is heard first as 'assess what is right', not 'give right judgements'. The adverb keeps the root of *rectus* (→ *reto*) and says the sense. *com retidão* (MS1932) would spend *retidão*, which is diréctio's word (glossary).

options.label: o que é reto
options.note: the object kept, parallel to *falais justiça*; DRB 'right things'.

options.label: com retidão
options.note: MS1932; *retidão* is diréctio's in the glossary.

decisions.why: ἀπηλλοτριώθησαν: 'were made strangers, estranged'. The cognate *se alienaram* is heard in Brazil as 'lost touch with reality / became politically alienated'. *tornar-se estranho* keeps the root the glossary gives *aliénus* (→ *estranho*), so the Latin family stays one family. MS1932 *perverteram-se* interprets. Draft 2 takes the stylist's order (both *desde* phrases fronted, a chiasm) and *se fizeram estranhos*, which drops the two enclitics side by side; the blind reader heard *estranhos* as 'odd people' — the cost of the *aliénus* row, weighed against a cognate heard as modern jargon.

options.label: se alienaram
options.note: the cognate; DRB 'are alienated'; heard as a modern word.

decisions.why: *erráre → extraviar-se* (row, which names 57:4). With the *desde* phrase fronted (the stylist's order) the pronoun goes before the verb: *se extraviaram*.

options.label: erraram
options.note: MS1932; *errar* is heard first as 'made a mistake'.

decisions.why: Two words for the womb (ἀπὸ μήτρας … ἀπὸ γαστρός). The glossary gives *úterus → seio materno* (21:11; *útero* is clinical, bare *seio* is the breast), so *ab útero* follows it. *vulva* is new; the Portuguese cognate is only anatomical. *ventre* is the plain biblical word for the womb (*desde o ventre*), and it is venter's in the glossary — but *venter* is not in this psalm, so nothing collides here. The two nouns stay two. The stylist (v2) proposed bare *desde o seio* to shorten the colon; refused: the *úterus* row exists because bare *seio* is the breast. It stays an option.

options.label: o ventre … o seio
options.note: stylist; shorter; bare *seio* is heard as the breast (row *úterus*).

options.label: o seio materno … o ventre
options.note: the two swapped; breaks the *úterus* row.

options.label: o nascimento … o ventre da mãe
options.note: MS1932's paraphrase (*desde o seu nascimento … desde que saíram do ventre de sua mãe*).

decisions.why: ἐλάλησαν ψεύδη; ψεῦδος is also the Greek of *mendácium* (5:7a *loquúntur mendácium* → *falam mentira*, singular there as the Latin), so by D15's test the two Latin words may share *mentiras*. *falaram falsidades* (MS1932 *disseram*) keeps the Latin's adjective root but makes a *fal- fal-* jingle at the close of a verse; *disseram falsidades* avoids it by spending *dizer* on *loqui*, which this psalm has just rendered *falar* (57:2).

options.label: mentiras
options.note: Ruling; the Greek's word, the *mendácium* row.

decisions.why: A verbless line with a dative of possession: 'fury to them according to the likeness of the serpent'. The copula is supplied (D2) and *similitúdo* kept as a noun — here it is ὁμοίωσις, likeness, not the byword of 43:15 (παραβολή → *termo de comparação*). The next colon hangs on it: *como a da áspide* (the likeness of the asp). *furor → furor* (row *ira / furor*); DRB 'madness', the Hebrew 'venom' — the Latin says fury. *deles* rather than *seu*, which after *serpente* could be read as the serpent's. Draft 2 takes the stylist's *é semelhante ao*: *é à semelhança* is a calque with a hiatus, and the feminine *a da áspide* sent the blind reader back to *serpente*. The root of *similitúdo* stays (*semelhante*); a noun turning adjective is grammar (D2). *o da áspide* now picks up *furor*, as the Latin's genitive picks up the likeness.

options.label: O furor deles é semelhante ao … como o

forms.furor: O furor deles é semelhante ao

options.label: O furor deles é à semelhança … como a

forms.furor: O furor deles é à semelhança

options.label: Eles têm um furor à semelhança … como a

forms.furor: Eles têm um furor à semelhança

decisions.latin: vocem incantántium: * et venéfici incantántis sapiénter
decisions.why: One verb twice (ἐπᾳδόντων … the charmer), so one root twice: *encantadores … encanta*. After the asp, *encantadores* is heard as snake-charmers, the Latin's sense; alone it could be 'charming people'. *venéficus* (φαρμάκου … φαρμακευομένου) is a poisoner-sorcerer (L&S): *feiticeiro* is the plain word; *envenenador* keeps the poison and loses the spell; *mago* (MS1932) is a Magus. *et* in a negative sentence → *nem* (grammar); *a do* repeats *voz*, which *venéfici* depends on. *sapiénter → sabiamente* (D43).

options.label: encantadores … nem a do feiticeiro … encanta
encantadores … nem a do mago … encanta
encantadores … nem a do envenenador … encanta
options.note: the poison of *venénum* in the word; the spell lost.

decisions.latin: Deus cónteret dentes eórum in ore ipsórum: * molas leónum confrínget Dóminus
decisions.why: The *contérere* row asks 57:7 to match 3:8 *quebrastes os dentes*: *quebrará os dentes*. *confríngere* is also *quebrar* in its row, except where it stands beside *contérere* — 45:10 decided the pair *quebrará … despedaçará*, because the Greek has two verbs there. Here too the Greek has two (συνέτριψεν … συνέθλασεν), so the same split. *molas*: L&S cites this verse for 'jawbone, or the teeth'; μύλας are grinders — *molares* keeps the teeth parallel to *dentes*; MS1932 *queixadas* (jaws) is the option. *in ore ipsórum* → *na própria boca*, so that *deles* is not said twice and *seus* cannot be heard as God's.

options.label: quebrará … molares … na boca deles
options.note: the *confríngere* row's default; one verb twice where the Latin and Greek have two.

decisions.latin: Ad níhilum devénient tamquam aqua decúrrens
decisions.why: *devenire ad níhilum*, 'come down to nothing'; the Greek is a passive, ἐξουδενωθήσονται, 'be set at nought', the verb of 14:4a *ad níhilum dedúctus est* → *reduzido a nada* (glossary). The Portuguese phrase *reduzir a nada* serves both; the intransitive *chegarão a nada* keeps the Latin's voice but is heard as 'will achieve nothing'. *decúrrens* → *que corre* (DRB 'running down'); 57:9 *fluit* → *que escorre*, so the two Latin verbs stay two.

options.label: Serão reduzidos a nada … que corre
options.note: Ruling; MS1932 *Serão reduzidos a nada*; the Greek's passive.

options.label: Chegarão a nada … que corre
options.note: the Latin's active voice; heard as 'come to nothing = fail'.

options.label: Serão reduzidos a nada … que passa

decisions.why: *inténdit* is present or perfect (the same letters); the Greek is a future (ἐντενεῖ). Both Vulgate-family witnesses read the perfect (DRB 'hath bent', MS1932 *entesou*). The subject is not named (God, from 57:7; MS1932 supplies *o Senhor* in a parenthesis, his gloss) and stays unnamed, as the Latin. *inténdere arcum → armar o arco* (row); *infirmári → enfraquecer* (row *infírmus*). The Latinist (v1, minor) asks for the present: the verbs around it are futures (*devénient*, *auferéntur*, *cónteret*), which makes the present the more natural reading. Taken; the perfect of the two Vulgate witnesses is the option.

options.label: retesa
options.note: the Latinist's verb; exact but little known (row *inténdere arcum*).

decisions.why: *fluere*, 'flow'; the Greek ὁ τακείς is 'melted'. Wax that flows is wax melting, and *escorre* keeps the Latin's image of flowing, which MS1932 *que se derrete* explains. *auferre → tirar* (D41): *serão tirados*, 'taken away'.

options.label: escorre … serão levados
options.note: plainer for 'taken away', but *levar* is addúcere's (D42).

decisions.why: *super-cádere*, 'fall upon', with no object named (ἐπέπεσε πῦρ). *de cima* renders the prefix without supplying an object; MS1932 has both (*caiu fogo de cima sobre eles*); *sobre eles* supplies the pronoun the Latin leaves to the context. The Latinist (v1, minor): *super-* is where the fire falls (upon), not whence; *de cima* turned it round. *cair sobre* needs its object in Portuguese, so *eles* is supplied, as DRB and MS1932 do; *sobreveio* (the Latinist's) loses the falling.

options.label: de cima
options.note: draft 1; nothing supplied, but the preposition turned round.

decisions.why: The darkest line of the psalm, and the Latin is the Greek word for word (πρὸ τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς ἀκάνθας ὑμῶν τὴν ῥάμνον): 'before your thorns understood the buckthorn' — commonly read as 'before your thorns grow into a thorn-bush', but neither the Latin nor the Greek says 'grow'. Kept as it stands: *intellégere → entender* (row), *spina → espinho* (31:4). *rhamnus* is a thorny shrub (L&S 'buckthorn'); *espinheiro* is the plain name; *ramno* is unknown; *sarça* (MS1932) is the Burning Bush. DRB 'could know' → *conhecessem* is the option. MS1932 *se convertam numa sarça* interprets.
*vivéntes* agrees with *eos*: 'swallows them as living men'. The preposition *a* marks it as the object in Portuguese.

decisions.latin: sicut vivéntes, sic in ira absórbet eos
decisions.why: *absórbet* is a present (the future would be *absorbébit*), 'swallows up' (καταπίεται). *tragar* is exact, but its present *traga* is also the subjunctive of *trazer* ('may bring them'). *engolir* is the plain verb for 'swallow'. *devorar* (MS1932) is 'devour', a beast's eating, a step from the Latin. The subject is unnamed, as the Latin; *eos* (the Greek has ὑμᾶς) is kept third person. Draft 2 adds *a* before *vivos* (the stylist): it ties *sicut vivéntes* to the object *eos*, as the Latin's accusative does.

decisions.latin: Si útique est fructus justo: * útique est Deus júdicans eos in terra
decisions.why: *útique* (ἄρα … ἄρα) twice, as the frame of the last line, and once in 57:2 (decision `vere`). *de fato* is plain and serves all three. MS1932 has *deveras … é certo* (two words for one), DRB 'indeed … indeed'. *Deus* without an article in the Latin; Portuguese needs *um* to say 'there is a God who judges' (*há Deus* is heard as a bare exclamation of faith).

options.label: de fato … de fato … um Deus

decisions.why: The blind reader heard draft 1's *quando vir* as the infinitive *vir*, 'when vengeance comes'. *ao ver* (MS1932's build) cannot be misheard and is two syllables shorter; the future-perfect nuance of *víderit* is carried by *se alegrará*.

options.label: ao ver
options.note: Ruling (v2, from the ambiguity reader); MS1932.

choices.57:2: Plural humans (the *fílii hóminum*, judges) are *vós* (decided); God is not addressed anywhere in this psalm. *fílii hóminum → filhos dos homens* (row *fílius hóminis*), vocative without *ó* as the Latin has none. *justítiam loquímini → falais justiça*: the content object kept, as the *loqui mendácium* row does. Matins antiphon for this psalm in DO is *Juste judicáte * fílii hóminum* (Psalmi matutinum) — other words from the verse, not a text of the psalm; not rendered here.
choices.57:3: *Étenim → Pois* (row). *operári iniquitátem → praticar a iniquidade* (row), plural kept. *concinnáre → tramar* (D44; its row names 57:3). *injustítia → injustiça*, apart from *iníquitas* (row) — the two stand in one verse here, as ἀνομίας / ἀδικίαν do.
choices.57:5: *obturáre → tapar*, the plain verb for stopping ears; *aures → ouvidos* (row *inclína aurem*). *et obturántis* keeps its *e*: the asp is deaf *and* stops her ears.
choices.57:6: *exaudíre → escutar* (D3), future kept (*escutará*). The verse continues the sentence of 57:5 (relative *Que*).
choices.57:11: *lætári → alegrar-se* (row), in the natural order rather than the mesóclise; *lavar as mãos* may ring as Pilate's idiom to the blind reader — it is the Latin's image; *vindícta → vingança* (the row's plural at 17:48 is that verse's own number); *sanguis* singular here as in the Latin.
choices.57:12: *homo* generic: *o homem*, as the Latin and DRB ('man shall say'). *os* (the Latin's *eos*) has no near antecedent, as in the Latin — the sinners of 57:10–11.
choices.57:10: The blind reader found *os vossos espinhos entendessem o espinheiro* incomprehensible, as the Latin and the Greek are; kept (decision `intellegerent`). The subject of *engole* is unnamed, as in the Latin.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm57.txt, 11 prayed verses (57:2–57:12), one mediant each, no flex. No titulus (D7). Liturgical uses searched with ps032/uses.py: no text of the psalm is used as antiphon or versicle; the Matins antiphon *Juste judicáte * fílii hóminum* is a free form of 57:2. Not a psalm of the day hours, so no Diurnal Monástico column.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps057.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings and rows applied: D2, D3 (*escutará*), D41 (*tirar*), D43 (*sabiamente*), D44 (*tramar*), rows *contérere* (57:7 named), *erráre* (57:4 named), *úterus* (57:4 named), *inténdere arcum* (57:8 named), *étenim*, *operári iniquitátem*, *injustítia*, *aliénus*, *fílii hóminum*, *ira / furor*, *infirmári*, *intellégere*, *spina*, *lætári*, *vindícta*, *mendácium*. Hard readings: 57:2 *vere útique*; 57:4 two words for the womb; 57:7 *molas*; 57:8 *inténdit* present or perfect; 57:10 the thorns and the buckthorn.

Draft 1: hard pass (ids and marks). Soft length flags accepted: 57:3a −3 (the Latin's long words, *iniquitátes operámini*); 57:4a +10 — the longest colon of the psalm in the Latin already (21), and it carries two verbs and two nouns for the womb; the *úterus* row's *seio materno* (two words for one) and *tornar-se estranhos* (a verb and a predicate for *alienáti sunt*) cost the rest; no shorter faithful build found (*se alienaram* saves one syllable and is heard as a modern word). 57:6b +3 (*nem a do* repeats the governing noun); 57:7b +4 (*despedaçará*, *molares*, five and three syllables); 57:9a +3; 57:10a +4 (*espinheiro* for *rhamnum*); 57:11a +3 (*quando vir* for *cum víderit*); 57:12a +4 (the article *o* and *para o* supplied). Cadences: all colons end paroxytone or oxytone.

audit.note: v2: 57:4 fronted chiasm *Desde o ventre os pecadores se fizeram estranhos, desde o seio materno se extraviaram*; 57:5 *é semelhante ao … como o da*; 57:8 *arma* (present); 57:9 *caiu fogo sobre eles*; 57:10 *como a vivos*; 57:11 *ao ver*. Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.

Draft 2: hard pass. 57:11a flag gone (*ao ver*). 57:4a still +10 by the counter (which does not elide *desde‿o*, *seio‿materno*): the fronted order shortens it in the mouth, not on the count; accepted for the reasons of draft 1. Other flags as draft 1.
claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, read latin.json. Gate clean of majors: three minors, all held (each is an option already).

outcomes.reason: Held: ψεύδη is the Greek of *mendácium* too (D15's test), and *falaram falsidades* jingles at the close; v1's gate passed *mentiras*.
*escorre* renders *fluit* in the next verse; the two Latin verbs stay two. *corre* is DRB's 'running'.

outcomes.remark: supercecidit: 'sobre eles' supplied; back to 'de cima'
outcomes.reason: The v1 gate asked for the opposite (*de cima* turns the preposition round) and v2 was made from that remark; the gate contradicts itself between runs (cf. D24). *cair sobre* needs an object; *eles* are the sinners of 57:9a, as DRB and MS1932 read. *de cima* stays option 1.
